summary: While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. content: What do Jesus and Isaiah have in common? Quite a bit, according to renowned British New Testament scholar N. T. Wright. Gathering at the marvelous Lanier Theological Library in Houston, Texas—the brainchild of noted attorney, author, and biblical scholar Mark Lanier—Wright offered a packed house in the Great Room a fascinating glimpse into the relationship between the Old Testament prophet Isaiah and the life, ministry, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Dr. Joseph Holden of Veritas International University listening to Dr. NT Wright at Lanier Library. For Wright, Isaiah is far more than an ancient prophetic voice whose words occasionally appear in the New Testament. Rather, the prophet provides a theological framework for understanding Jesus and the unfolding purposes of God. In his book Into the Heart of Isaiah , Wright invites readers to rediscover the extraordinary depth of Isaiah’s prophetic vision, demonstrating how its themes of judgment, restoration, redemption, and new creation find their ultimate expression in Christ. Central to Wright’s interpretation is the conviction that Isaiah’s message cannot be separated from the larger story of Israel. The prophet speaks of exile and homecoming, divine judgment and covenant faithfulness, suffering and salvation. These themes, Wright argues, become essential to understanding how Jesus understood his own mission and how the earliest Christians interpreted his life. Particularly significant is Isaiah’s portrayal of the suffering servant, whose affliction becomes the means through which God’s redemptive purposes are accomplished. Wright connects this prophetic imagery to Jesus’ sacrificial death, while emphasizing that the cross cannot be isolated from the broader biblical promise of God’s restoration of creation. Equally important is Isaiah’s vision of a renewed world, a creation in which justice, righteousness, and peace flourish under God’s reign. For Wright, the resurrection of Jesus announces the beginning of that promised new creation. The Christian hope, therefore, is not simply an escape from the present world, but the ultimate renewal of God’s good creation. Personal Stories: Mounting Up with Wings Like Eagles Amid the theological insights and biblical exposition, Wright shared several personal stories, offering the audience a glimpse into how the words of Isaiah have shaped not only his scholarship but also his spiritual imagination. One story centered on the beloved passage from Isaiah 40:31, in which the prophet declares that those who wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength and mount up with wings like eagles. Wright recalled preaching on Isaiah many years earlier and drew an amusing comparison to the long-running British radio program Desert Island Discs , in which notable guests select the recordings they would take with them if stranded on a deserted island. “I’ve sometimes said I have a set of desert island texts,” Wright explained, suggesting that certain biblical passages remain especially meaningful throughout one’s life. Near the top of his list, he said, is the closing portion of Isaiah 40, with its magnificent image of soaring eagles. The passage, he suggested, is more than a favorite theological text. It is part of his personal testimony, a biblical promise that has accompanied him through the years. A second story brought the imagery of Isaiah into an unexpected encounter with the natural world. While completing the final proofreading of Into the Heart of Isaiah , Wright and his wife, Maggie, were staying at their home in Scotland. Wright was alone in a room, carefully reviewing the text, when something outside caught his attention. “Out of the corner of my eye, I saw something,” he recalled. “At first, I thought it was somebody’s dog that had come into our front garden.” Noted Biblical archeologist, Dr. Steven Collins, listening to Mark Lanier interview Dr. NT Wright at Lanier Library. But it was no dog. It was a white-tailed eagle, one of th

content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .

title: In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words
summary: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star, the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of […]  The post  In the shadow of western stars: Grover Lewis, Larry McMurtry, and the triumph of words  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. title: Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage
summary: By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own […]  The post  Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. title: Offended by foul language on food show
summary: By Charles Gardner — We used to be regular viewers of the The Great British Bake-Off TV series, now being screened on Channel 4, celebrating the efforts of amateur contestants in the kitchen. My wife is qualified in home economics and once, in her far-off student days, helped Mary Berry out over the weekend. I […]  The post  Offended by foul language on food show  first appeared on  God Reports .
content: By Charles Gardner — We used to be regular viewers of the The Great British Bake-Off TV series, now being screened on Channel 4, celebrating the efforts of amateur contestants in the kitchen. My wife is qualified in home economics and once, in her far-off student days, helped Mary Berry out over the weekend. I too like to lend a hand with my cooking skills. So when, the other day, we were intrigued to see how new presenter Nigella Lawson was doing on the show, we switched it on – and were truly appalled at the foul language spewing out of the mouths of at least two contestants. Taking the name of the Lord Jesus Christ in vain, they loudly expressed their frustration (rather than praise) at things going wrong with their concoctions in front of more than seven million viewers. We switched it off, vowing to complain in the strongest possible terms, which I have since done. And though it’s hard to be surprised at the language regularly heard on television programmes these days, I was shocked to the core by Channel 4’s response, basically saying that this particularly offensive blasphemy doesn’t come under the category of “strong language”. Really? It’s surely the worst of them all. “We are sorry to hear you were offended by some of the language used within the programme,” they wrote. “Whilst we do appreciate that you find the use of such phrases or words unacceptable, we are not obliged under the Ofcom code to obscure them, nor do they fall under the category for strong language. We therefore have no obligation to bleep them either pre- or post-watershed.” I had suggested that they could at least have edited them out, adding that they were being very hypocritical as they wouldn’t have allowed swearing in the name of Mohammed, a point which they ignored. Have we sunk so low in our nation that there is nothing left that is sacred, except woke left-wing ideology and appeasement of those who hate the God of Israel and his Son Jesus, our Lord? But we have forsaken the God who brought peace and prosperity to Britain, and who saved us from Nazi invasion, for the idols of food and celebrity. Shame on us! Is it not time the Christian world woke up and stood against this flood of filth in our midst, which will sweep us away into the oblivion of a third-rate country if we do not act soon. Where has the ‘land of hope and glory’ gone? The ‘mother of the free’ we sing about at the Proms, calling on the God ‘who made thee mighty’ to ‘make thee mightier yet’? The Apostle Paul was surely prophesying the decline and fall of the Roman Empire in his letter to the early Christians in Rome (a mixture of Jews and Gentiles), when he wrote: “The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness, since what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them. For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities – his eternal power and divine nature – have been clearly seen, being understood from what has been made, so that men are without excuse.” (Romans 1:18-20) The post Offended by foul language on food show first appeared on God Reports .

title: Kehilangan yang Membawa Berkah
title_zh: 带来祝福的失去
content: Oleh: Gevonny Dinda Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Gevonny Dinda, biasa dipanggil Dinda. Sebagai orang Kristen, saya merasa bersyukur dilahirkan di dunia ini dan berkesempatan untuk mengenal Tuhan Yesus. Saya sungguh bahagia dapat merasakan berkat-Nya setiap hari dan sangat bersyukur akan apa yang Tuhan Yesus berikan kepada saya selama ini. Kabar baik, kabar buruk, cobaan, dan berkat, saya terima dengan penuh rasa ucapan syukur. Di sini, saya akan menceritakan salah satu berkat Tuhan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada 19 Februari 2015, saya menerima kabar buruk bahwa kakek saya telah berpulang ke rumah Tuhan. Kepergian kakek saya sangat membekas di hati banyak orang, terutama nenek saya. Nenek saya sangat merasa kehilangan karena memang nenek belum siap menghadapi hal ini sehingga membuat kondisi badannya melemah. Sejak ditinggal kakek, kondisi mental dan fisik nenek saya semakin memburuk. Awalnya, ia merasa sangat kesepian dan merasa takut jika ditinggal sendirian di rumah. Bahkan, nenek saya sering menangis jika merasa kesepian. Ibu saya dan ketujuh saudara kandungnya akhirnya sepakat untuk bergantian menjaga nenek saya di rumahnya supaya tidak merasa kesepian lagi. Setelah itu, hari-hari nenek saya berjalan normal seperti biasa. Namun, karena umurnya yang bertambah tua, kondisi fisiknya semakin melemah. Sejak 2017, nenek saya sudah tidak kuat lagi berjalan dan harus memakai kursi roda. Di situlah, ketabahan dan kesabaran anak-anaknya, termasuk ibu saya, diuji dalam mengurus nenek saya. Pakde, budhe, tante, dan om saya yang hidup di luar kota, seperti: Jakarta, Yogyakarta, dan Kudus, semakin sering menyempatkan diri pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bergiliran mengurus nenek saya. Sampai pada April 2018 lalu, kondisi nenek saya berada di titik terburuknya. Karena anak-anaknya sudah memiliki firasat yang tidak baik, mereka memutuskan untuk berkunjung bersama-sama ke rumah nenek saya. Mereka hanya bisa berdoa bersama untuk kondisi ibu mereka. Sampai pada akhirnya, Tuhan Yesus memanggil nenek saya untuk ikut bersama-Nya. Karena sudah siap dengan kepergian nenek saya, kami semua menerima kepergian nenek dengan sukacita dan penuh ucapan syukur karena nenek saya sudah sembuh dan pergi ke tempat yang lebih indah, menyusul kakek saya. Tidak disangka, kepergian kakek dan nenek saya membawa berkah bagi keluarga besar kami. Tuhan Yesus memiliki kuasa untuk membuat keluarga kami menjadi lebih dekat satu sama lain. Hubungan anak-anak beserta cucu-cucu mereka menjadi lebih dekat. Kakak-kakak Ibu saya yang dahulu sering pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bertemu dan menjenguk orang tua mereka, sekarang lebih menghargai waktu kebersamaan dengan keluarga yang diberikan oleh Tuhan. Sejak saat itu, kami semua memiliki satu grup chat dan sering menanyakan kabar satu sama lain. Bahkan, kami semua memiliki keinginan untuk lebih sering bertemu pada masa depan, dan melakukan kegiatan bersama-sama seperti berlibur dan arisan keluarga. Semua itu tidak pernah terjadi sebelum kepergian kakek dan nenek saya, dan saya sungguh percaya Tuhan Yesus turut campur tangan dalam semua kejadian yang menimpa keluarga saya. Ia tidak pernah berhenti untuk menunjukkan betapa sayangnya Ia terhadap anak-anak-Nya, bahkan ketika anak-anak-Nya sedang berada dalam keterpurukan. Tuhan Yesus selalu memiliki rencana yang indah untuk setiap anak-anak-Nya, dan saya sangat percaya Ia telah memberikan sesuatu yang besar untuk membalas rasa kehilangan keluarga saya selama ini. Tuhan Yesus memang sungguh baik! Semoga Tuhan selalu memberkati keluarga Anda!

title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. title: Kembali Kepada Jalan Tuhan
title_zh: 回归主的道路
content: Nama saya Yoel, saya adalah seorang mahasiswa semester terakhir dari salah satu universitas swasta di Jawa Tengah. Saya dilahirkan dalam keluarga Kristen. Ibu dan Bapak saya cukup baik dalam membimbing saya untuk tetap dalam jalan Tuhan. Penyertaan Tuhan itu baik dalam kehidupan saya. Baiklah, saya akan ceritakan apa dosa yang sudah pernah saya lakukan. Rokok, pornografi, dan buang-buang waktu adalah keseharian saya pada waktu saya duduk di bangku SMU. Pada waktu itu, saya merasa ada yang kosong dalam hidup saya, tepatnya tidak ada gairah untuk mencapai suatu tujuan. Saya tidak merencanakan masa depan, pokoknya hidup terus mengalir. Sebenarnya, saya tertarik dengan dunia perfilman, saya ingin menjadi sutradara, tetapi ayah saya tidak mengizinkannya karena dia tidak melihat ada bakat seni dalam diri saya. Menurutnya, orang seni hanya akan mendapat uang atau pengakuan jika karyanya diterima. Kalau tidak mendapat pengakuan, ya "habis". Itulah perkataan ayah saya, saya masih ingat jelas. Menurut saya, dosa itu nikmat. Namun, saya juga sadar bahwa itu hanya kenikmatan sesaat. Saat saya masih SMU kelas satu, selama setahun saya merokok, tetapi saya benar-benar tidak dapat merasakan kenikmatannya. Mungkin itu hanya alat bagi saya supaya diterima oleh teman-teman saya. Saya suka mencoba hal baru, mungkin itu juga motivasi saya saat itu. Namun, jangan salah paham, teman-teman saya tidak pernah memaksa saya ikut merokok. Akhirnya, saya berhenti merokok saat kelas dua. Sebelumnya, sejak SMP kelas tiga, saya sudah kecanduan pornografi. Video porno begitu menarik bagi saya. Keinginan untuk melihat adegan dewasa itu sangat kuat. Ketika kuliah, pada tahun kedua, saya mulai berusaha serius untuk menghentikan kebiasaan tersebut. Saya mulai berpikir tentang dampak buruk pornografi secara serius. Menurut saya, sepertinya hanya saya yang ingin benar-benar lepas dari pornografi dalam lingkup pertemanan saya. Teman-teman saya sepertinya menerima hal itu sebagai sesuatu yang normal. Saya pun juga berusaha menerimanya sebagai sesuatu yang normal, tetapi saya tidak bisa berpikir seperti itu. Pasti ada dampak buruknya, saya yakin itu. Salah satu dampak buruk yang sudah saya rasakan adalah rendah diri. Saya selalu merasa diri saya itu "sampah". Dampak lainya adalah ketika saya melihat lawan jenis, saya akan cenderung menjadikannya objek seks. Itu sungguh menghancurkan martabat manusia sebagai makhluk yang berakal budi. Saya merasa kalau saya menonton video porno dan onani (ini sangat umum dalam dunia remaja), Tuhan akan membenci saya dan tidak menganggap saya lagi. Saya pernah berpikir untuk meninggalkan Tuhan dan hidup sesuka hati saya. Suatu saat, pernah saya berpikir bahwa saya sudah terlalu berdosa sehingga tidak bisa diperbaiki. Namun, Yesaya 1:18 menyadarkan saya bahwa Tuhan selalu menerima pertobatan manusia, tidak peduli seberapa buruk dosa yang sudah dilakukannya. Dalam kelemahan saya, Tuhan seolah-olah berkata, "Tidak apa-apa, Nak, bangun dan jangan berhenti." Pada tahun ketiga kuliah saya, sebenarnya saya sudah bisa lepas dari pornografi, dalam arti tidak kecanduan, tetapi tetap ada satu atau dua kali saya tergoda. Saya juga mengisi beberapa tahun dalam hidup saya kecanduan gim (game). Saat SMP, gim PS2 membuat saya menghabiskan uang jajan saya. Saat SMU dan kuliah, gim komputer membuat saya lupa waktu. Memang gim ini menjadi suatu pelampiasan akan rasa rendah diri saya. Selain bermain gim, aktivitas lain yang saya kerjakan adalah makan dan mandi. Saya tidak peduli akan hal lain. Tentu saja, sekarang saya menyesal, berapa banyak waktu yang saya buang. Alangkah baiknya jika dahulu saya melakukan sesuatu yang produktif, seperti mengasah kemampuan dalam bidang tertentu. title: Pertolongan yang Tidak Pernah Terlambat
title_zh: 永远不会迟到的帮助
content: Oleh: Odysius B. Temara Bersyukur untuk kasih karunia Tuhan yang selama ini tidak henti-hentinya saya rasakan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada kesempatan kali ini, saya ingin berbagi tentang kisah pengalaman hidup saya. Semasa kuliah, saya merasa bahwa saya adalah salah satu orang yang paling beruntung karena hampir selalu mendapatkan kemudahan dalam studi saya. Saya mendapatkan dosen-dosen yang ramah, teman-teman yang selalu mendukung saya, bahkan para staf akademik yang sangat bisa diajak bekerja sama. Semuanya berjalan sesuai dengan apa yang saya rancangkan sampai tiba-tiba segalanya berubah ketika saya menginjak semester akhir. Saya sangat terkejut ketika mengetahui bahwa saya diberi dosen pembimbing yang terkenal sangat sulit untuk penulisan skripsi saya. Beliau adalah salah satu dosen yang paling sibuk dan paling susah untuk dihubungi, terlebih untuk konsultasi. Pernah sampai tiga minggu beliau keluar kota, sakit, dan terlalu sibuk dengan tugas-tugas mengajar sehingga skripsi saya menjadi terbengkalai karena saya tidak bisa berkonsultasi dengan beliau. Ketika saya sedang berkonsultasi dengan beliau, sering kali beliau juga menyelipkan kalimat-kalimat sarkastik yang terkadang membuat saya lebih tertekan lagi. Seiring berjalannya waktu, teman-teman saya mulai lulus satu per satu, dan saya masih terjebak. Pada saat itu, saya merasa sangat kesal karena skripsi saya tidak kunjung selesai. Bukan karena saya yang malas-malasan, tetapi karena sulitnya menemui dosen pembimbing saya. Saya sempat mempertimbangkan untuk pindah pembimbing, tetapi rasanya sangat sayang kalau harus mulai dari awal lagi. Saya menceritakan keluh kesah saya kepada orang tua saya. Ayah saya menyarankan saya untuk lebih giat lagi berdoa, serahkan semuanya kepada Tuhan. Saya berdoa kepada Tuhan supaya Dia melembutkan hati dosen pembimbing saya dan juga memberi kekuatan dan kesabaran untuk saya dalam menghadapi beliau. Hari demi hari, saya berdoa dan sedikit demi sedikit tampak mulai terjadi perubahan pada sikap dosen pembimbing saya. Perubahan sikap itu tidak hanya terjadi kepada saya, tetapi juga kepada anak bimbingannya yang lain. Akhirnya, dengan proses yang cukup panjang, saya berhasil menyelesaikan skripsi saya dan lulus pada 12 Agustus 2014. Meskipun rancangan saya gagal untuk bisa lulus dalam 3,5 tahun, saya merasa bersyukur karena pertolongan Tuhan tidak pernah terlambat bagi saya sehingga saya masih bisa lulus tepat waktu. Sampai sekarang, saya senantiasa mengucap syukur kepada Tuhan atas segala yang Tuhan izinkan terjadi dalam kehidupan saya. Saya menyadari bahwa seberat apa pun permasalahan hidup yang saya hadapi, tangan kuat Tuhan akan selalu ada untuk menuntun saya melewatinya.

title: Merasakan Kasih Natal
title_zh: 感受圣诞节的爱
content: Natal merupakan liburan yang paling istimewa bagi ayah saya. Persiapan menjelang Natal, berbelanja hadiah, dan menghias rumah tidak membuatnya lelah - bahkan ia sangat menikmatinya. Ibu bercerita, ayah memperkenalkan saya dengan pohon Natal saya yang pertama waktu saya masih berusia sembilan hari. Pohon Natal itu kecil, tetapi setiap hiasan, lilin, dan untaian perada perak digantungnya dengan sangat teliti pada tempatnya, seolah-olah hanya ia yang dapat melakukannya. Setelah selesai, ayah mengangkat saya dari keranjang buaian dan menggendong saya supaya melihat hasil pekerjaan tangannya. Ayah masih menghias empat pohon Natal sesudah itu dan setiap kali pohonnya lebih besar dari tahun sebelumnya. Pada hari ia meninggal -- tak lama setelah menderita radang paru-paru -- ibu duduk dengan saya membicarakan Natal. "Madeline," katanya lembut, "Sinterklas akan memberikan hadiah untukmu, tetapi kita tidak mempunyai pohon dan hiasannya. Tahun ini pengeluaran kita sudah terlalu banyak." Besok hari Natal, tetapi sampai pagi ini tidak ada persiapan khusus untuk keesokah harinya, selain kebaktian pagi dan makan malam di rumah salah seorang anggota keluarga. Menjelang sore, telepon berbunyi dan ibu mengangkatnya. Tidak lama kemudian saya mendengar ibu berkata, "Anda baik sekali, tetapi rasanya kami akan melewatkan malam Natal di rumah. Natal ini pertama kali sejak ..." Lalu ibu dapat melanjutkan lagi, berterima kasih kepada penelepon itu sekali lagi dan menutup pembicaraan. "Siapa Bu?" tanya saya. "Salah seorang tetangga kita," kata ibu. "Ia mengundang kita malam ini. Ibu ... Ibu tidak bisa." Ibu diam saja hampir sepanjang hari. Sorenya, ibu berubah pendapat. Ia menelepon tetangga kami, mengatakan kami akan mampir sebentar. "Dia baik sekali," kata ibu kepada saya, "dan kita tidak mau dianggap tidak menghargainya." Setelah kami membunyikan bel pintu rumah tetangga kami, nyonya rumah menyambut dan mencium kami, lalu mengantar kami melewati serambi. Ruang tamu kelihatannya gelap, tetapi anehnya ada cahaya yang berwarna-warni. Ia mengajak kami masuk, dan saya melangkah ke dalam ruangan dan terperangah. Di sana, di tengah taburan lampu yang berwarna-warni dan bermacam-macam hiasan, lengkap dengan hadiah-hadiah yang dibungkus dengan kertas wama-warni yang cerah, berdiri sebuah pohon Natal yang indah sekali. Di sekeliling pohon itu duduk Ny. Abrams, Ny. Cohen, Ny. Blount, Ny. Dreyfus, sambil tersenyum lebar. "Selamat datang!" sapa mereka serempak. Sampai sekarang saya dapat memejamkan mata dan mengingat kisah tersebut dengan jelas. Sering ingatan itu menguatkan saya apabila keadaan memburuk, waktu saya meragukan hati manusia. Saya masih dapat merasakan kasih tetangga kami -- kaum ibu Yahudi yang mengambil risiko untuk melaksanakan tradisi yang tidak mereka kenal supaya seorang anak Kristen yang sudah tidak mempunyai ayah tetap dapat bergembira merayakan Natal. - Madeline Weatherford | Dipublikasikan | : | http://natal.sabda.org |

content:
교인들 부담 낮추려 수준도 낮춰 초대교회, 철저한 변화 목표 교육 산상수훈 실천 반문화 대안 사회

기독교학술원(원장 김영한 박사)은 지난 11월 12일 ‘섬김의 영성’을 주제로 임원 사경회를 용인 포도나무교회(담임 여주봉 목사)에서 개최했다.

매년 11월 진행되는 사경회에는 임원 부부와 함께 기독교학술원 ‘영성 아카데미’ 영성수사 과정 수료 수사 7명이 참가해, 성령 안에서 진지한 학문적 담론을 이어갔다.

개회예배에서 이사장 여주봉 목사는 ‘탈기독교 시대 전도 어떻게 해야 하나?’라는 제목으로 메시지를 전했다. 그는 “반기독교 정서가 심해지고 있는 오늘날 한국교회는 엄청난 세속주의의 쓰나미를 맞설 준비가 전혀 되지 않았다”며 “목회자들은 교인들이 아무런 부담감 없이 쉽게 교회에 올 수 있도록, 거의 모든 것을 초신자 수준으로 낮춰버렸다”고 개탄했다.

여주봉 목사는 “4세기 이전 초대교회는 성경대로 교인들이 매우 높은 기준의 삶을 살도록 양육했기에, 엄청난 박해와 순교 위협 속에서도 오히려 성장했다”며 “기독교가 공인된 313년 로마 제국 내 그리스도인 비율은 20%가 넘었다”고 지적했다.

여 목사는 “초대교회가 놀랍게 성장할 수 있었던 핵심 요소로 학자들이 공통적으로 동의하는 부분은 교회와 성도들의 변화된 삶에서 풍겨져 나오는 매력과 자유함이었다”며 “초대교회 문헌들에는 복음 전도에 대한 목회적 권고가 전혀 나오지 않지만, 팀 켈러의 말처럼 당시 불신자들이 볼 때 초대교회는 산상수훈을 실천하는 ‘반(反)문화’ 공동체로서 매력적인 대안 사회였다”고 설명했다.

그는 “초대교회는 예비 신자들을 교회 정회원으로 받아들이기에 앞서 3년 이상 양육했다. 단순한 교리교육에서 멈추는 것이 아니라, 산상수훈 수준의 철저한 삶의 변화를 목표로 양육했다”며 “오늘날 한국교회도 이를 본받아야 한다”고 제언했다.

이번 임원사경회에서는 총신대와 대신대 총장을 역임한 정성구 박사가 특강을 전했다. 그는 존 칼빈의 ‘소명의 영성’과 아브라함 카이퍼의 ‘봉사의 영성’을 소개했다.

정성구 박사는 “카이퍼에 의하면 ‘소명 없이 헌신 없고, 헌신 없이 참된 봉사는 없다’. 목사나 선교사뿐 아니라 모든 신자는 각기 하나님께로부터 부르심을 받은 자들(고전 7:20)”이라며 “신자는 하나님께 헌신하기를 요구받는다(롬 12:1). ‘무슨 일을 하든지 마음을 다하여 주께 하듯 하고 사람에게 하듯 하지 말아야 한다(골 3:23-24)’”고 밝혔다.

정 박사는 “칼빈의 소명론에 따르면, 신자가 가진 재능과 직업과 재산은 이웃을 위해 사용해야 할 하나님의 선물”이라며 “카이퍼에 의하면 ‘인간의 삶은 하나님과 무관한 영역이란 한 곳도 없다. 모든 삶의 영역에서 그리스도께서 주인이시다. 그러므로 소명은 봉사의 방향을 정하고, 헌신은 봉사의 동력을 제공하며, 봉사는 소명을 현실 속에서 실천한다’”고 전했다.

그는 “카이퍼의 소명론과 기독교 문화관에 따르면, 우리는 ‘교회에서 얼마나 봉사했는가?’라는 질문을 넘어서 이렇게 질문해야 한다”며 “나는 가정에서 하나님을 섬기고 있는가? 나는 직장에서 하나님을 섬기고 있는가? 나는 학문을 통해 진리를 섬기고 있는가”라고 했다.

정성구 박사는 전도사 시절 간증도 전했다. 그는 당시 시골에 가서 가마니 깔고 예배를 드리기 시작했고, 모든 마을 주민을 ‘내 교인’이라는 마음으로 대했다. 교회는 부흥 성장해 3년 만에 예배당을 지었다. 이후 마을 사람들과 함께 기쁨으로 헌당예배를 드렸다고 한다. 그는 카이퍼의 말로 특강을 마무리했다. “우리의 소명은 세상 한가운데 있고, 바로 여기서 하나님은 영광을 받으셔야 한다.”

기독교학술원장 김영한 박사는 ‘창세기 1-3장에 대한 창조신학적 해석 : 창조론에 대한 개혁신학적 착상’이라는 제목으로 강의했다. 그는 “오늘날 유신진화론 내지 진화론적 창조론’을 말하는 이들은 과학적 증거가 결여된 ‘자연주의적 진화론’과 타협하는 경향을 보이고 있다”고 지적했다.

김영한 원장은 “개혁신학 전통 속 성경적 창조론 입장에 확고히 서서, 다윈의 진화론과 자연선택설, 멘델 유전학, 집단유전학을 결합한 이론인 신다윈주의와 그 전제를 수용하는 유신진화론에 반대한다”며 “성경무오를 견지하면서도 타락 전 동물의 죽음 가능성을 인정하는 점진적 창조론 즉 ‘오래된 지구 창조론(Old Earth Creation)’과 문자적 6일 창조를 전제하는 ‘젊은 지구 창조론(Young Earth Creation)’에 대해서도 비판적”이라고 했다.

김 원장은 “우주와 세상 기원의 사건은 하나님이 주권적으로 행하시는 계시적 원형 역사적 사건(proto-historical event)”이라며 “창세기 1-3장의 창조와 인간 기원·본성·타락 내러티브를 역사적 사실성에 대한 계시적 명제로 받아들이되, 계시적 문장이 문학적·구속사적으로 묘사됐다는 특징을 인정해야 한다”고 방향을 제시했다.

끝으로 “(중간단계 화석을 통한 입증이 결여된) 진화론은 무신론적 인본주의를 바탕으로 잘못된 지식과 가설로 만들어진 이론”이라며 “개혁주의적 창조론은 열려 있는 태도를 가지면서도, ‘계시 우위적 사유’ 원리에 충실한 가운데 무분별한 타협을 경계해야 한다”고 덧붙였다.

기독교학술원 이사이자 변증신학자인 박명룡 목사(청주서문교회)는 ‘기적, 오늘날에도 일어나는가?’라는 제목으로 특강을 전했다. 그는 “현대인이 기적을 믿지 못하는 이유는 과학의 옷을 입은 무신론적 자연주의 세계관 때문”이라고 진단했다.

박명룡 목사는 “사람이 창조주 하나님에 대힌 신앙을 가지게 되면 세계관이 바뀌고, 자연스럽게 하나님이 간섭하시는 세계 속에서 다양하고 풍부한 기적을 경험하게 된다”며 수많은 기적 사례들에 대한 조사를 소개했다.

퓨 포럼(Pew Forum)의 조사에 의하면 직·간접적 신적 치유 경험자가 약 2억 명이고, 미국인 중 38%는 하나님의 기적을 체험했다고 한다. 연구에 의하면 최근 수십 년간 세계 개신교 성장의 약 70%가 ‘기적 경험’에 기인하고, 박해 속에서도 급성장한 중국 교회 성도들 90%가 치유를 경험했으며, 개신교가 급성장중인 브라질 성도들도 86%가 치유를 경험했다. 최근 무슬림 회심이 매년 1백만 명 이상 이어지는데, 그들 중 50-70%도 사도행전적 기적을 경험하고 있다고 한다.

박 목사는 “기적을 믿는 것이 반드시 비과학적이거나 비지성적인 태도는 아니다. 중요한 것은 처음부터 ‘지적은 일어날 수 없다’고 결론을 내리는 것이 아니라, 실제로 어떤 사건이 일어났으며 그것을 가장 잘 설명하는 것은 무엇인지를 열린 마음으로 살펴보는 것”이라며 “세상을 창조하신 하나님이 실제로 존재하신다면, 당신이 창조한 세계에 특별한 방법으로 개입하시는 것은 얼마든지 가능하다”고 강조했다.

summary_zh: 一位伊朗基督徒女性正在开展一项特殊的传教工作，她前往墓地，向那些失去亲人、沉浸在悲痛中的人们传扬福音。她在什叶派穆斯林的哀悼文化中经历了信仰的转变，为了将自己所发现的喜乐与希望传达给他人，她定期前往墓地。韩国殉道者之声（Voice of the Martyrs Korea，以下简称韩国VOM）近日介绍了在伊朗开展活动的基督徒女性帕拉斯图（Parastoo，出于安全考虑使用化名）的信仰历程和传教工作。帕拉斯图（Parastoo）在伊朗长大，从小就与家人一起定期参加伊斯兰宗教仪式和什叶派节日活动。然而，对于她来说，宗教仪式带给她的更多是悲伤和沉重，而非喜悦。她目睹了什叶派穆斯林为哀悼侯赛因·伊本·阿里（Husayn ibn Ali）的逝世而举行的宗教仪式，她的家人也前往清真寺
title_zh: 伊朗基督徒女性通过“墓地布道”向悲痛之人传福音
content:
이란의 한 기독교인 여성이 가족을 잃고 슬픔에 잠긴 사람들을 찾아 묘지에서 복음을 전하는 특별한 선교 사역을 이어가고 있다. 시아파 무슬림의 애도 문화 속에서 신앙의 변화를 경험한 그는, 자신이 발견한 기쁨과 소망을 다른 사람들에게 전하기 위해 묘지를 정기적으로 방문하고 있다.

한국순교자의소리(Voice of the Martyrs Korea, 이하 한국VOM)는 최근 이란에서 활동하는 기독교 여성 파라스투(Parastoo·보안상 가명)의 신앙 여정과 선교 사역을 소개했다.

어린 시절 이란에서 자란 파라스투는 가족과 함께 이슬람 종교의식과 시아파 절기 행사에 정기적으로 참여했다. 그러나 그에게 종교 행사는 기쁨보다 슬픔과 무거움을 느끼게 하는 시간이었다. 시아파 무슬림들이 후세인 이븐 알리(Husayn ibn Ali)의 죽음을 애도하며 종교의식을 치르는 모습을 지켜봤고, 가족들 역시 이슬람 사원에서 돌아올 때마다 슬픔에 잠겼다고 회상했다.

한국VOM 현숙 폴리 대표는 이러한 애도 문화가 7세기 후세인의 죽음과 관련돼 있다고 설명했다. 시아파 무슬림들은 후세인이 무함마드의 정당한 후계자가 됐어야 했다고 믿으며, 그의 죽음에 대한 슬픔과 신앙적 헌신을 종교의식으로 표현해 왔다는 것이다.

파라스투는 이러한 분위기 속에서 점차 이슬람 신앙에 회의를 느꼈다. 그는 마음속으로 하나님과 같은 존재를 믿으며 “하나님, 제가 인생에서 기쁨을 느낄 수 있게 해주세요”라고 기도했다.

그의 삶이 변화한 것은 20대 시절 아버지와 함께 외국으로 여행을 갔을 때였다. 현지 기독교인들의 초대로 교회를 방문한 파라스투는 이전에 경험하지 못했던 분위기에 놀랐다. 슬픔 대신 기쁨이 있었고, 성도들은 함께 기도하며 서로 격려하고 안아 줬다. 특히 기타 반주에 맞춰 성경 말씀을 노래하는 모습이 인상적이었다.

교회를 방문할 때마다 흰옷을 입은 남자가 나타나 “내 손을 잡고 내 이름을 부르렴”이라고 말하는 꿈을 꾼 그는 친구들과 목회자에게 꿈에 관해 이야기했다. 이들은 그리스도께서 자신을 따르도록 부르시는 것이라고 설명했고, 파라스투는 예수님을 믿기로 결심했다. 그의 아버지도 함께 기독교인이 됐다. 파라스투는 “마침내 제 길을 찾았다. 참된 길이신 예수님을 찾은 것”이라고 말했다.

이란으로 돌아온 뒤 파라스투는 남편 델샤드(Delshad·보안상 가명)와 함께 기독교 신앙을 비밀리에 이어갔다. 이후 교회에서 구한 성경과 기독교 서적을 친구들에게 나누며 복음을 전하기 시작했다.

그러던 중 그는 슬픔에 잠긴 사람들에게 소망의 메시지를 전할 장소로 묘지를 떠올렸다. 첫 번째 묘지 전도에서 울고 있는 한 여성을 만난 파라스투는 “제가 안아 드려도 될까요? 하나님이 당신의 마음을 슬픔에서 기쁨으로 바꿔주시도록 기도해도 될까요?”라고 물었다. 그 여성을 위해 기도하고 소망에 관한 기독교 자료를 전달하자, 여성은 도움이 필요한 순간 하나님께서 파라스투를 보내주셨다고 말했다.

파라스투는 “그 여성은 슬픔과 눈물을 안고 묘지에 왔지만, 기쁨과 소망을 품고 떠났다”고 회상했다. 이후 묘지 방문은 정기적인 사역으로 자리 잡았다. 그는 “제가 열망하는 것은 사람들이 참되신 하나님이 누구신지 깨닫는 것이다. 할 수만 있다면 모든 사람을 돕고 싶다”고 말했다.

그러나 복음 전파는 당국의 감시와 조사로 이어졌다. 2022년 정부 관리들은 파라스투를 소환해 며칠간 심문했다. 기독교 자료의 보관 장소와 다른 기독교인들과의 접촉 여부, 이슬람 사원에 나가지 않는 이유 등을 추궁했다.

구금 13일째 되던 날 파라스투는 기도 중 하나님의 임재를 느꼈으며, 시편 23편의 “여호와는 나의 목자시니”라는 말씀을 떠올렸다고 전했다. 다음 날 조사 담당관은 16쪽 분량의 문서를 내밀며 서명하지 않으면 간첩 혐의를 받게 될 것이라고 위협했다. 문서에는 다른 기독교인과의 만남과 예배를 포함한 모든 기독교 활동을 중단한다는 내용이 담겨 있었다. 그는 구금에서 벗어나기 위해 결국 서명했다.

석방 이후에도 박해는 계속됐다. 남편 델샤드는 공무원직에서 해고됐고, 부부는 새 일자리를 구하는 데 어려움을 겪었다. 정부 요원들은 기독교인을 비방하는 선전 활동에 참여하도록 요구했지만, 남편은 이를 거부했다. 이후 요원들이 자택을 급습해 파라스투의 휴대전화와 노트북을 압수하기도 했다.

현숙 폴리 대표는 “이란에서 기독교로 개종한 사람들은 배교 혐의로 기소돼 사형에 처해질 수도 있어 신앙을 공개하기 어렵다”고 설명했다.

이러한 위험에도 파라스투는 오늘날까지 묘지와 여러 장소에서 여성들을 만나 기도하고 복음을 전하고 있다. 그는 자신과 남편이 하나님의 평강 속에서 담대하게 살아가고, 더 많은 이란 사람이 예수님을 알게 되도록 기도해 달라고 요청했다.

현숙 폴리 대표는 “파라스투가 시편 1편 3절에 나오는 나무처럼 많은 열매를 맺고 결코 시들지 않기를 소망하고 있다”고 전했다. 파라스투는 “그 사람들을 위해 기도해 달라. 더 많은 사람을 찾아가 기쁨을 전해줄 수 있도록 기도해 달라”고 당부했다.
